content.text: The profile shows one change: `plan_code` has a new value, `GOLD`, on 8 of 24 rows, which the contract's `allowed` list rejects. Everything else matches. I'll validate the edit (add `GOLD`, bump the version) and check the dry run.

input.contract_yaml:
# Member eligibility from a (synthetic) payer: one row per member, one file per day.
# Generated from the Synthea patients by packs/healthcare/generators/eligibility.py.
feed: healthcare.eligibility
version: 2
owner: vendor-ops@example.com
description: >
  Daily full eligibility file: every enrolled member with their plan and coverage dates.
  All data is synthetic.
classification: restricted
source:
  channels: [minio, sftp, api]
  filename_pattern: "elig_*.csv"
  # The business date in the name (elig_YYYYMMDD.csv). It must be a real date, not after
  # the day the file was received, and at most 7 days before it; otherwise the file is
  # quarantined (FILE.NAME_DATE). A name with no digits takes the date it was received.
  filename_date:
    regex: "^elig_([0-9]+)"
    format: "%Y%m%d"
    max_days_before_received: 7
    max_days_after_received: 0
format: { type: csv, delimiter: ",", encoding: utf-8, header: true }
expected_arrival: { cron: "0 6 * * *", grace: 2h }
on_row_violation: quarantine_row
max_bad_row_ratio: 0.05          # above this, the whole file is rejected
min_rows: 1
columns:
  - { name: member_id, type: string, required: true, unique: true, pattern: "^M[0-9]{9}$" }
  - { name: first_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: last_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: dob, type: date, required: true, min: "1900-01-01", max: today, phi: true }
  - { name: sex, type: string, required: true, allowed: [F, M, U] }
  - { name: plan_code, type: string, required: true, allowed: [HMO, PPO, EPO, HDHP, GOLD] }
  - { name: coverage_start, type: date, required: true, min: "1990-01-01" }
  - { name: coverage_end, type: date, description: "Empty while coverage is open" }
  - name: patient_ref
    type: string
    description: The payer's link to the clinical record (here the Synthea patient id)
    phi: true

input.rationale: Drift in elig_20261021.csv (job 1): the vendor added a new plan tier, GOLD, on 8 of 24 rows. It is a clean, consistent plan label with no other column changes (no missing, unexpected or reordered columns; all other rules pass), so I read it as a deliberate product change, not junk. Without the change, 8/24 rows (33%) would fail the allowed list, far above max_bad_row_ratio 0.05, so the whole file would be rejected. Change: plan_code allowed list gains GOLD; version 1 -> 2. Loosening: plan_code.allowed now accepts GOLD. Reason: the file proves GOLD is a valid, intended plan code for good data. Nothing else changed. Not changed but flagged for review: member_id is labelled phi: true by the profile but is not marked phi in the contract. Under the drift rules existing columns keep their phi setting, so I left it as is; a person should decide whether it should become phi: true, since it identifies a member. Dry run: 24 accepted, 0 rejected, file not rejected.

content.text:
The vendor's file added a new plan tier, `GOLD`, on 8 of 24 rows. It is a clean, consistent label, and no other columns changed, so I treated it as a deliberate product change.

- **Contract change:** `plan_code` now allows `GOLD` (in addition to HMO, PPO, EPO, HDHP), and the version goes from 1 to 2.
- **Loosening:** `plan_code.allowed` gains `GOLD`. Without it, 33% of rows would fail, well above the 5% limit, so the whole file would have been rejected.
- **Dry run:** 24 accepted, 0 rejected, file not rejected. Candidate `e4d8a99990deee94` is submitted for review.
- **Flag for a person:** the profile labels `member_id` as PHI, but the contract doesn't mark it. Drift rules keep existing column settings, so I left it alone. Someone should decide whether it should become `phi: true`.
